domain.title: Home electricity use
domain.summary: One day of electricity use in a home, measured every 10 minutes (144 values). The model says if the day looks like a warm-season day or a cold-season day, and marks the hours that made it decide - for example heating in the evening.
domain.data_note: The examples come from the PowerCons test set (UCR archive): one household's electricity use over a year, split into days. Warm season = April to September, cold season = October to March. The model never saw them while training. The dataset does not say at what time a day starts. The average day is lowest at 02:00-06:00 and highest at 20:00-22:00, which fits a day that starts at midnight, so the clock times shown assume that.

classes.label: Warm season
classes.description: The day looks like one from April to September: less heating, lower use in the evening.

classes.label: Cold season
classes.description: The day looks like one from October to March: more heating and lighting, higher use in the evening.

model_card.architecture: The same SEA-Net design as the other domains (sea_mstcn_sep_bottleneck + sea_topk_conjunctive), trained only on PowerCons.
model_card.how_it_explains: The model gives every 10-minute step a score for each class. The final score of a class is the average of its strongest 10% of steps. Those per-step scores are what you see shaded on the chart.
limitations: Trained on ONE household. Other homes use power in other ways.
It only knows two groups (warm / cold season) - it does not find faults.
The test set is small (180 days), so the accuracy number can move a few points with other data.
Several days in a row are cut into 144-value windows, one per day if the file starts at midnight.
